title: Support/resistance zones — non-blocking review follow-up from PR #164
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #164 (backend-support-resistance-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: PR #164's efficiency refactor (splitting `detect_support_resistance_zones`'s scoring into a cheap `_score_candidate` used for ranking, and `_build_zone` now only run on the top-`max_zones` survivors) is provably equivalent to the old pipeline by code inspection -- the sort key (`strength_score`, `touch_count`, `last_touch_date`) never depends on the deferred `_scan_breaks_and_false_breakouts`/`_dollar_volume` work, and pr-reviewer independently re-verified this both by re-reading the code and via a standalone synthetic simulation of 40 candidates confirming old-pipeline vs new-pipeline produce identical order/truncation. However, `backend/tests/unit/signals/test_support_resistance.py`'s only zone-cap test (`test_max_zones_caps_the_returned_list`) exercises a single qualifying candidate with `max_zones=1` -- it truncates a list of length 1 and never exercises reordering across multiple distinct-strength-score candidates, so it would NOT catch a ranking-order regression in this exact refactor if one were ever introduced (e.g. a future edit to the sort key or the score/build split). Add a fixture with >`max_zones` (15) qualifying candidate clusters spanning multiple `strength_score` values (varying length/height category combinations) and assert `detect_support_resistance_zones`'s returned zones are both capped at `max_zones` AND in strict descending (`strength_score`, `touch_count`, `last_touch_date`) order, to give this refactor's equivalence claim real, in-repo regression coverage instead of relying on external reasoning alone.
